question: Do commercial text-embedding models represent scalar decimal and signed values as a clean continuous one-dimensional magnitude, and how does that representation change with precision, sign, and scale?

key_findings.claim: A linear probe can usually recover sampled scalar values with high fidelity, so numeric information is present even when the embedding geometry is not itself one-dimensional.
key_findings.evidence: Across Google Gemini, three OpenAI models, and three Voyage models, five-fold linear-regression experiments report R-squared at or above 0.95 for the positive-decimal condition in the tabulated minima, while mixed signs and large magnitudes reduce some models substantially.

key_findings.claim: The leading principal component captures only a minority of embedding variance despite often tracking numerical order.
key_findings.evidence: The first-component explained-variance ranges in Table 1 remain below 0.40 for every positive-decimal model, whereas the paper's PCA-value correlations can be much higher. The authors interpret the remaining directions as variation orthogonal to the scalar input rather than evidence that the scalar cannot be decoded.

key_findings.claim: Increasing decimal precision and introducing signs expose model- and provider-specific discontinuities rather than a uniform degradation law.
key_findings.evidence: The precision sweeps show decreasing reconstruction and PCA metrics for several OpenAI and Gemini variants, while some Voyage explained-variance curves increase; mixed-sign PCA often separates sign first and magnitude second. The integer-scale table also shows Gemini's minimum linear R-squared falling to 0.48 while other providers stay above 0.89.

key_findings.claim: The experiments diagnose isolated numeral-string embeddings, not whether a language model can use quantities correctly in context or on a downstream retrieval task.
key_findings.evidence: Each dataset contains at most 500 randomly sampled scalar strings per precision condition and the evaluation consists of post-hoc linear reconstruction and PCA; no contextual sentences, unit-sensitive retrieval judgments, causal intervention, or arithmetic task is evaluated.

method.core_idea: Embed controlled sets of scalar strings and test whether their high-dimensional geometry preserves the ordinal, one-dimensional structure of the source numbers.
method.mechanism: For positive decimals, mixed-sign decimals, and mixed-sign values with increasing integer digits, the study fits five-fold linear probes from embeddings to scalars, correlates the first principal component with the scalar, and measures that component's explained variance across seven commercial embedding models.
assumptions: A clean continuous scalar representation should be linearly decodable and concentrated along a leading principal direction.
Formatting a number as an isolated string is a meaningful proxy for numerical representations used inside scientific text applications.
Provider APIs and their undocumented tokenization/model revisions are stable enough for cross-model comparison.

techniques.role: Varies decimal places, integer places, and sign while holding the semantic object—a scalar—fixed.
Measures whether a simple affine map can reconstruct magnitude from the full embedding.
Separates alignment of the leading axis with magnitude from how much total embedding variation that axis explains.

evaluations.setting: Positive decimals in [0,1], one through twenty decimal places, at most 500 samples per condition, seven commercial embedding models
evaluations.metric: Five-fold linear R-squared, first-PC correlation R-squared, and first-PC explained variance
evaluations.result: Minimum linear R-squared is 0.95 or higher for all models; maximum first-PC explained variance stays at or below 0.36.
evaluations.baseline: An ideal one-dimensional continuous representation would make both reconstruction and leading-component concentration approach one.

evaluations.setting: Mixed-sign decimals in [-1,1] across precision levels
evaluations.result: Minimum linear R-squared ranges from 0.85 to 0.99; PCA plots frequently organize sign separately from magnitude.

evaluations.setting: Mixed-sign values with increasing integer digits
evaluations.metric: Linear and PCA extrema across the sweep
evaluations.result: Gemini reaches a 0.48 minimum linear R-squared and a negative minimum PC correlation, while OpenAI and Voyage variants retain minimum linear R-squared of 0.89 or higher.

limitations: Author-stated: only a small set of provider-specific embedding models is tested, and the proposed metrics do not prescribe the nonlinear geometry that a useful number representation must have.

Reviewer inference: low first-component explained variance is labeled noise without a matched text-string control, so tokenizer, formatting, and representational features useful in context may contribute to the residual.
Reviewer inference: the random scalar datasets and five-fold probe share the same formatting distribution, leaving extrapolation and out-of-distribution precision untested.
failure_modes: A model may encode magnitude accurately on a nonlinear periodic manifold and therefore look discontinuous under PCA while supporting reliable numerical computation.
A high-capacity embedding can linearly expose scalar magnitude yet rank numerically inappropriate neighbors under cosine similarity; reconstruction alone does not validate retrieval behavior.
Silent provider model updates can change embeddings and make the reported comparisons difficult to reproduce.
reusable_insights: Evaluate decodability and geometric concentration separately: high probe accuracy does not imply a simple or distance-preserving representation.
Precision, sign, and order of magnitude should be independent axes in numerical-representation benchmarks.
A useful follow-up should pair geometric probes with unit-aware retrieval and causal numerical tasks.
open_questions: Do contextualized numerals with units exhibit the same sign and precision geometry as isolated scalar strings?
Which embedding distances or learned calibrators preserve relative numerical error across many orders of magnitude?
Are residual principal directions tokenizer artifacts, semantic-format features, or causally used components?

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Know the Value of Numbers
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhu et al. probe whether numeric values are encoded in language-model representations; this paper instead audits commercial embedding endpoints across decimal precision, sign, and magnitude with both reconstruction and PCA concentration metrics.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Encode Numbers Using Digit Representations in Base 10
competitive_landscape.difference: Levy and Geva identify causal digit-wise circular representations inside language models, whereas the reviewed work treats endpoint embeddings as black boxes and asks whether scalar geometry is globally continuous.

competitive_landscape.title: What is a Number, That a Large Language Model May Know It?
competitive_landscape.difference: Marjieh et al. distinguish value- and string-based similarity structures in number representations; the reviewed paper operationalizes impurity through linear reconstruction, leading-PC correlation, and explained variance over precision sweeps.

competitive_landscape.title: Pre-trained Language Models Learn Remarkably Accurate Representations of Numbers
competitive_landscape.difference: Kadlcik et al. use nonlinear sinusoid-aware probes to recover numbers almost exactly from open-model embeddings; that result directly cautions against interpreting poor linear/PCA geometry as absence of precise numeric information.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this is a lightweight, task-independent audit of continuous scalar fidelity across commercial embedding providers and precision/sign/scale regimes. Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: the controlled precision sweep and joint reporting of decodability versus explained variance are useful, but the broad title overstates what black-box isolated-string PCA establishes; nonlinear-probe and causal work already shows that complex geometry can retain precise numeric content.
reviewer_notes: Read against all twelve extracted pages, including figure-only appendix pages. Quantitative statements above are author-reported; claims about missing contextual, causal, and retrieval validation are reviewer inferences. Competitor records were checked on their primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
